products.title: Myriophyllum Mattogrossense
products.body_html:
Myriophyllum mattogrossense is one of the finest-textured background plants available — bright green feathery whorls on slender stems that move with the current. It fills a back wall faster than almost anything else, which is both the appeal and the thing to plan for.

What You'll Receive

Sold as loose fresh-cut plants, bunched plants, or potted plants:

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Approximately 6 individual, loose-cut stems without root
  • Bunched Plants: Approximately 6 stems without root bundled with foam and a plant weight
  • Potted Plants: Approximately 6 stems without root potted in rockwool and net pot

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Mattogrossense Milfoil
  • Scientific name — Myriophyllum mattogrossense
  • Also known as — Green Milfoil, Brazilian Milfoil
  • Origin — Mato Grosso, Brazil
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Mature height — 8-16 inches
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.0-7.0
  • Substrate — Nutrient-rich soil helps, but it feeds mainly from the water column
  • Growth habit — Amphibious stem
  • Propagation — Cuttings

Grower's Notes

  • It feeds from the water, not the substrate. Root tabs do little here. Consistent water column dosing — macros and iron — is what keeps the whorls dense and the green bright.
  • Low light makes it leggy, not dead. Under weak lighting the internodes stretch and the feathering thins out. That is a light problem, not a nutrient one.
  • Fast growth means it shades its neighbors. At eight to sixteen inches and growing quickly, it will overtop anything planted in front of it within weeks. Trim on a schedule rather than when it looks untidy.
  • Handle it gently — the foliage is brittle. Fine whorls shed easily when pulled through water or gravel. Plant stems individually with tweezers rather than pushing a bunch in by hand.
  • Trim and replant the tops. Lower stems go bare as the canopy thickens. Cutting the top few inches and replanting them keeps a background even and doubles your stem count.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Myriophyllum (Milfoil) Care Guide.

Notes

  • Myriophyllum mattogrossense is a fast-growing plant that may require regular trimming to prevent shading other plants. Under low light, stems may become leggy.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Java Fern Latifolius
products.body_html:
The widest leaf in the genus. Latifolius means broad-leaved, and this Java Fern earns it — flat, expansive blades on an upright plant that reaches over a foot. Where narrow-leaf forms give a scape fine texture, this one gives it mass.

What You'll Receive

Sold as loose bare-root plants, bunched plants, or potted plants:

  • Bare-root Plants: Approximately 3+ leaf portion, loose rhizome
  • Bunched Plants: Approximately 3+ leaf portion bundled with foam and plant weight
  • Potted Plants: Approximately 3+ leaf portion, potted in rockwool and net pot

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Latifolius Java Fern
  • Scientific name — Leptochilus pteropus 'Latifolius' (syn. Microsorum pteropus)
  • Origin — Cultivated form; the species is native to Southeast Asia
  • Placement — Midground to background, attached to driftwood, stone or décor
  • Mature height — 8-14 inches
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5, soft to moderately hard
  • Substrate — Not required. Epiphyte — attach the rhizome to hardscape and never bury it.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious; grows emersed as well as submersed
  • Propagation — Rhizome division, plus plantlets from mature leaves

Grower's Notes

  • Big leaves are efficient coverage. Java Fern is priced per plant, not per area. On a large piece of wood, one Latifolius covers ground that would take three or four narrow-leaf plants — and it does it without CO₂ or bright light.
  • Broad leaves catch more light, so shade matters more. The wide blade intercepts everything above it, which is good for coverage and bad for algae. Keep it out of the brightest part of the tank and the leaves stay clean.
  • Never bury the rhizome. Roots may go into substrate; the green horizontal stem must stay in open water or it rots — the single most common way a Java Fern is killed.
  • Wipe the leaves at water changes. A large surface on a slow plant collects debris it cannot shed. A gentle thumb-and-finger wipe every few weeks keeps it dark green.
  • Black spots on old leaves are baby plants, not disease. Leave a spotted leaf in place until each plantlet has roots and two or three leaves, then detach and attach it elsewhere.

Looking to buy in bulk? Get 10 or 20 plants in one order with our Java Fern Latifolius Bulk Pack and save 40–50% per plant.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Java Fern Care Guide.

Notes

Photos are sample representations. Actual plants may vary in size, shape, or coloration. Unless otherwise specified, we do not guarantee plants are free of pests, pesticides, or exclusively submerged-grown.

Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Giant Duckweed
products.body_html:
Duckweed you can actually remove. Spirodela polyrhiza has fronds several times the size of common duckweed and much longer trailing roots — which means it nets out in sheets instead of scattering, while still delivering the fast nutrient export and surface shade floaters are bought for.

What You’ll Receive

A small portion (approximately 2” × 2”) of healthy Giant Duckweed containing 10+ plants.

Plants are carefully harvested and packed to ensure they arrive fresh and ready to add directly to your aquarium or pond.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Giant Duckweed
  • Scientific name — Spirodela polyrhiza
  • Placement — Free-floating on the surface
  • Size — Fronds roughly 0.2–0.4 in across
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required. It takes CO₂ from the air
  • Water — 65–85°F · pH 6.5–7.5
  • Substrate — Not required
  • Growth habit — True aquatic, free-floating
  • Propagation — Natural division

Grower’s Notes

  • Size is the practical advantage over common duckweed. Lemna minor is nearly impossible to remove once established because every 2mm frond repopulates the tank. Spirodela is big enough to net out properly — the same benefits with a working undo button.
  • Long roots make better fry and shrimp cover than common duckweed's stubby ones.
  • Surface flow packs it into corners where it rots. Aim filter returns downward or add a floating ring.
  • Thin it at every water change or it seals the surface and starves plants below of light.
  • Common duckweed often travels with floating plants — check a new portion before adding it if you're keeping the tank Lemna-free.

Notes

  • Pictures are sample representations. Portion size and frond count vary naturally.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Bucephalandra Biblis Blue Sky
products.body_html:
Biblis Blue Sky is one of the strongly iridescent Bucephalandra varieties — narrow, wavy-edged leaves that throw blue, turquoise and violet reflections depending on the angle you view them from. It stays under three inches, which makes it a nano plant with an outsized visual effect.

What You'll Receive

Sold as loose bare-root plants:

  • 1 Plant: Loose bare-root with approximately 6+ leaves
  • 5 Plants: Loose bare-root with approximately 25+ leaves total
  • 10 Plants: Loose bare-root with approximately 50+ leaves total

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Biblis Blue Sky Buce
  • Scientific name — Bucephalandra sp. 'Biblis Blue Sky'
  • Also known as — Buce Biblis Blue Sky
  • Origin — Borneo (genus range)
  • Placement — Foreground, attached to hardscape
  • Mature height — 1-3 inches
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium. Moderate light brings out the blue; under very low light the leaf reads plain dark green.
  • CO₂ — Not required, but it deepens color and speeds an otherwise slow plant.
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — None needed. Epiphyte; feeds from the water column.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious rhizome creeper; grows submersed or emersed
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower's Notes

  • The blue is structural, not pigment. It comes from the way the leaf surface reflects light, so it appears and disappears as you move around the tank and photographs unpredictably. Position it where viewers see it from an angle, not straight on.
  • Never bury the rhizome. Tie it to wood or rock and leave it exposed; buried rhizomes rot.
  • Farm-raised, not wild-collected. All the Bucephalandra we carry is farm-grown, and much of it is raised from tissue culture rather than collected from Borneo.
  • Some leaf melt after shipping is normal. The rhizome survives and pushes new submersed leaves within a few weeks.
  • Divide with a clean blade, keeping several leaves and some roots on each section.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Bucephalandra Care Guide.

Bucephalandra species are naturally slow growers and may experience minor leaf melt during acclimation. This is temporary — new, healthy leaves will develop as the plant adjusts to your aquarium environment.

products.title: Bacopa sp. Marble
products.body_html:
Variegation on the toughest stem plant there is. Bacopa monnieri 'Marble' marbles the thick rounded leaves of common Moneywort in green and white — the pattern of a collector's plant on a species famous for surviving anything.

What You'll Receive

  • Fresh-cut plants | 6 stems, loose fresh-cut plants
  • Bunched plants | 6 fresh-cut plants with foam, and lead weight.
  • Potted plants | 6 fresh-cut plants with net pot and rock wool.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Marble Moneywort
  • Scientific name — Bacopa monnieri 'Marble'
  • Also known as — Bacopa Marble, Bacopa Variegated, Marble Water Hyssop
  • Origin — Cultivated form; the species is pantropical
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — 6 fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 inches
  • Mature height — 6-12 inches
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. Brighter light sharpens the marbling
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required

  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich substrate supports the variegation
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed

Grower's Notes

  • Harder than plain Moneywort, but not hard. The white tissue carries no chlorophyll, so the plant produces less energy than the species and has less margin — hence Intermediate rather than Beginner. It is still Bacopa monnieri underneath, which means it forgives more than most variegated plants.
  • It can revert. Plain green shoots photosynthesize better and will slowly take over the group. Cut them out at the base as they appear.
  • Marbling needs light. Under weak lighting the pattern fades toward green and the plant loses the only reason to buy it over the standard form.
  • Trim above a leaf pair and replant the tops. Each cut branches the stem, which is how a few stems become a group.

products.title: Proserpinaca Palustris 'Cuba' (Mermaid Weed) Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
The leaves change shape, not just color. Proserpinaca palustris 'Cuba' — Mermaid Weed — arrives with smooth, plain green foliage from emersed growth, then produces finely toothed, needle-like leaves once submerged, warming to copper, orange and red under strong light. Few aquarium plants alter their form this completely, and the serrated texture is unlike anything else in a planted tank. This is the sterile Vitro Culture® (tissue culture) format.

What You'll Receive

  • 1 Pack Vitro Culture® (4-inch bag) containing multiple young plantlets
  • Each sterile culture can be gently separated into several individual plants ready for planting throughout your aquarium

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Mermaid Weed
  • Scientific name — Proserpinaca palustris 'Cuba'
  • Also known as — Cuba Mermaid Weed
  • Origin — North and Central America
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — 4-inch bag of small plantlets, smooth-leaved on arrival
  • Mature height — 6–14 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. Light intensity drives both the serration and the copper-red
  • CO₂ — Recommended for the best color and compact growth
  • Water — 65–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient substrate, plus water column dosing
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Smooth leaves emersed, serrated submerged
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower's Notes

  • Smooth leaves on arrival are correct. Emersed-grown Mermaid Weed has plain, untoothed foliage and looks nothing like the photographs. The serrated needle-like form appears only on new submerged growth — give it several weeks before judging it.
  • Light does two jobs here. It drives the copper-red color, and it also sharpens the serration. Under weak light the plant grows but stays green with softer, less defined leaf edges — losing both of the things it is bought for.
  • Rinse the gel off and separate the plantlets before planting, spacing them an inch apart. Planted as a clump the lower stems shade out.
  • Trim and replant the tops. Cuttings color and serrate faster than the stumps regrow.
  • It pairs well with Rotala and Ludwigia — similar warm tones, completely different leaf texture, which is what makes the grouping work.

Notes

  • Live aquatic plants naturally vary in size, coloration, and appearance depending on growing conditions and season. Plants may appear slightly different from photos after shipping but will adapt and develop their mature coloration once established in the aquarium.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Bucephalandra Centipede
products.body_html:
Centipede is named for its leaf arrangement — narrow leaves set closely along a creeping rhizome, so an established plant looks like a segmented line running across the rock rather than a rosette. It is one of the more distinctive growth forms in the genus.

What You'll Receive

  • Sold as a Bunched Plants or Potted Plants.
  • Pictures are not the actual plants you will receive, but a sample representation.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Centipede Buce
  • Scientific name — Bucephalandra sp. 'Centipede'
  • Also known as — Buce, Bucep
  • Origin — Borneo (genus range)
  • Placement — Foreground to midground, attached to hardscape
  • Mature height — 2-4 inches
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium. Too much light brings algae the plant is too slow to outgrow.
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — None needed. Epiphyte; feeds from the water column.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious rhizome creeper; grows submersed or emersed
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower's Notes

  • Mount it along a line, not in a clump. Centipede's appeal comes from the rhizome creeping in one direction with leaves spaced along it. Tie it lengthways down a branch or a stone edge and the pattern develops; bunch it up and you lose the effect entirely.
  • Never bury the rhizome. Tie it to wood or rock and leave it exposed; buried rhizomes rot.
  • Farm-raised, not wild-collected. All the Bucephalandra we carry is farm-grown, and much of it is raised from tissue culture rather than collected from Borneo.
  • Give it flow. Bucephalandra are rheophytes from fast Borneo streams, and moderate current keeps the leaves clean of debris and algae.
  • Some leaf melt after shipping is normal. The rhizome survives and pushes new submersed leaves within a few weeks.

products.title: Cryptocoryne Green Gecko Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Want a Crypt that stays bright green? Cryptocoryne 'Green Gecko' keeps a glossy lime-green with a lightly crinkled leaf surface, where most Crypts run bronze, brown or red. Against dark wood and red plants it reads as a genuine highlight. This is the sterile Vitro Culture® format.

What You’ll Receive

One 4-inch sealed Vitro Culture® bag containing healthy Cryptocoryne 'Green Gecko' plantlets — ready to rinse, acclimate, and plant.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Green Gecko Crypt
  • Scientific name — Cryptocoryne sp. 'Green Gecko'
  • Also known as — Cryptocoryne wendtii 'Green Gecko'
  • Placement — Foreground to midground
  • Mature height — 3–5 in
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium. Intense light is not needed
  • CO₂ — Not required, though it keeps growth more compact

Grower’s Notes

  • Green is the selling point. If you already have Wendtii Brown or a red Crypt and want contrast rather than more of the same, this is the one that supplies it — same easy care, opposite color.
  • Expect it to melt after planting. Crypts drop their leaves on a change of conditions and rebuild from the roots over two to four weeks. Leave it alone through that.
  • Feed at the roots and place it once. Crypts melt again every time they are moved.
  • Hard water is no obstacle. Cryptocoryne generally do well in harder water than most planted-tank species — if stem plants have disappointed you in hard tap water, Crypts are the group to try.
  • Rinse the gel off completely before planting or it clouds water and feeds algae in the first weeks.

Also available as loose bare-root plants if you want an established clump rather than plantlets.

products.title: Echinodorus Yellow Sun
products.body_html:
Most swords are green. 'Yellow Sun' comes through yellow-green, sometimes with orange or light red at the edges under stronger light — heart-shaped leaves that read as a warm patch rather than another block of dark foliage.

What You'll Receive

Enhance your aquarium with our fresh, high-quality plants, available in convenient formats:

  • Loose Bare-Root Plants: Includes approximately 1-2 loose, bare-root plants, providing flexibility in planting and arrangement.
  • Rooted Bunched: Approximately 1-2 plants, bundled with foam and a plant weight for easy placement.
  • Rooted Potted: Includes approximately 1-2 plants, potted in a net pot with rock wool, ensuring stability and ease of placement in your aquarium.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Yellow Sun Sword
  • Scientific name — Echinodorus 'Yellow Sun'
  • Also known as — Echinodorus cordifolius 'Yellow Sun', Golden Sun Sword
  • Origin — Cultivated form; parent species from the Americas
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Mature height — 10-16 inches
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.5-7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Heavy root feeder — nutrient-rich soil or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious rosette
  • Propagation — Adventitious plantlets on flower stalks

Grower's Notes

  • Light decides whether it is yellow or just green. Under medium light the leaves lean pale green; stronger light brings out the golden tone and the orange-red edging. This is the one variable worth adjusting if the color disappoints.
  • Root tabs are not optional. Swords take almost everything from the substrate. In inert gravel with liquid dosing alone the yellow washes out to a sickly pale green, which is easy to mistake for a deficiency in the water column.
  • Never bury the crown. Cover the roots and leave the growing point at substrate level. A buried crown rots from the center and does not recover.
  • It propagates from flower stalks, not runners. A mature plant sends up an inflorescence carrying plantlets along its length; let each root and grow three or four leaves before separating it.
  • Use it against green, not against red. Yellow-green next to red plants muddies both. Set against dark green foliage or wood it does what it is bought for.

products.title: Helanthium Vesuvius (Twisted Chain Sword)
products.body_html:
Vallisneria with a twist — literally. Helanthium bolivianum 'Vesuvius' grows narrow ribbon leaves, roughly 4 mm wide, that spiral tightly as they rise from a low rosette. Selected from a mutation of H. bolivianum 'Angustifolius' at the Oriental nursery in Singapore and in the trade since 2006.

What You'll Receive

Enhance your aquarium with our fresh, high-quality plants, available in convenient formats:

  • Loose Bare-Root Plants: Includes approximately 1–2 loose, bare-root plants, providing flexibility in planting and arrangement.
  • Rooted Bunched: Approximately 1–2 plants, bundled with foam and a plant weight for easy placement.
  • Rooted Potted: Includes approximately 1–2 plants, potted in a net pot with rock wool, ensuring stability and ease of placement in your aquarium.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Vesuvius Twisted Chain Sword, also known as Corkscrew Sword
  • Scientific name — Helanthium bolivianum 'Vesuvius'
  • Also known as — Echinodorus 'Vesuvius' (the older name)
  • Origin — Cultivated selection, Singapore; the species is native to South America
  • Placement — Foreground
  • Mature height — 3-6 inches
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.5-7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Root feeder — fine gravel, sand or aquasoil with root tabs.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious rosette; also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Runners. Unlike the true Echinodorus swords, chain swords genuinely do spread under the substrate.

Grower's Notes

  • It arrives straight and twists later. We grow it emersed, where the leaves are broader, shorter and barely curled. The tight spiral only develops on submerged growth — so the plant in the bag will not look like the photograph, and that is expected.
  • This one really does send runners. Chain swords are Helanthium, not Echinodorus: they spread under the substrate, rooting daughter rosettes a few inches from the parent. Leave each runner attached until the daughter has its own roots, then lift and move it.
  • Feed the roots. Root tabs or aquasoil under the planting area do far more than liquid dosing for a plant that feeds this way.
  • Use it where the movement shows. The spiral reads as motion in open water or gentle flow. Crowded between broad-leaved plants the effect disappears and a plain chain sword would do the same job.
  • Expect emersed leaves to melt back. Remove them once they yellow — it encourages the submerged rosette to fill in faster.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Helanthium Chain Sword Care Guide.

Notes

This plant is shipped in its emersed form. Upon submersion, the leaves will gradually transition into their final form—narrow, upright, and tightly twisted. Older emersed leaves may melt back, which is normal. Remove any unsightly leaves to encourage healthy submerged growth.

Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Hygrophila lancea 'Araguaia'
products.body_html:
Hygrophila lancea 'Araguaia' does not behave like the rest of its genus. Instead of racing to the surface it stays low and branches sideways, building compact bushes of narrow, needle-shaped leaves in bronze, brown and deep red. It is the rare Hygrophila you plant in the middle of a tank rather than behind everything.

What You'll Receive

Fresh, healthy Hygrophila lancea 'Araguaia' cultivated and prepared by Aquarium Plants Factory®, available in convenient planting formats:

  • Fresh Cut Plants: Approximately 6 loose, fresh-cut stems without roots.
  • Fresh Cut Bunched: Approximately 6 stems bundled with foam and a plant weight for easy placement.
  • Fresh Cut Potted: About 6 stems potted securely in a net pot with rockwool for stability and easy planting.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Araguaia Hygrophila
  • Scientific name — Hygrophila lancea 'Araguaia'
  • Also known as — Hygrophila Araguaia, Hygrophila 'Chai' relative
  • Origin — Collected from the Araguaia river basin, Brazil; the species itself is native to East Asia
  • Placement — Midground
  • Mature height — 4-10 inches
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — Nutrient-rich soil or root tabs, plus water column dosing
  • Growth habit — Amphibious stem, feeds from roots and water column
  • Propagation — Cuttings

Grower's Notes

  • It branches instead of climbing. Most Hygrophila needs constant topping to stay in the midground. Araguaia naturally throws side shoots and stays compact, so a planted group thickens on its own with far less trimming.
  • CO₂ changes the leaf shape. Without injection the leaves are broader and the growth looser. With it, they narrow into the fine needle form and the bush tightens — the difference is visible rather than subtle.
  • Color sits between bronze and red. This is not a scarlet plant. Under medium light with steady iron dosing it holds a brown-red tone that reads as depth against green neighbors, which is exactly what makes it useful.
  • Expect melt in the first two weeks. Emersed-grown stems drop most of their original leaves after planting. Leave the stems in place — the submersed growth that follows is the form you want.
  • Plant it where a stem plant would normally be too tall. At four to ten inches it fills the awkward gap between a carpet and a background hedge, which few red plants do well.

products.title: Brazilian Pennywort Marble
products.body_html:
Brazilian Pennywort is already one of the easiest stem plants sold. The marbled form keeps that and adds cream and pale green streaking across those round, lily-pad leaves — rare-looking foliage on a plant that grows fast enough to fill space in weeks.

What You'll Receive

Fresh, healthy Brazilian Pennywort Marble cultivated and prepared by Aquarium Plants Factory®, available in convenient planting formats:

  • Fresh Cut Plants: Approximately 4 fresh-cut stems without roots.
  • Fresh Cut Bunched: Approximately 4 stems bundled with foam and a plant weight for easy placement.
  • Fresh Cut Potted: About 4 stems potted securely in a net pot with rockwool for stability and easy planting.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Marble Brazilian Pennywort
  • Scientific name — Hydrocotyle leucocephala 'Marble'
  • Also known as — Hydrocotyle leucocephala 'Variegated'
  • Origin — Central and South America
  • Placement — Midground, or left floating
  • Mature height — 8-16 inches
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — Nutrient-rich soil or root tabs; also feeds from the water column
  • Growth habit — Amphibious creeping stem
  • Propagation — Runners

Grower's Notes

  • Variegated does not mean difficult here. Pennywort grows fast enough to carry the loss of chlorophyll without slowing down. It stays a beginner plant — the marbling costs you nothing in difficulty.
  • Solid green stems will appear. Any variegated plant can revert, and green growth is more efficient so it spreads if left. Cut reverted stems out at the base as you spot them.
  • It grows in three directions. Planted it climbs, floated it spreads across the surface, and laid against hardscape it creeps. Decide which you want and trim to enforce it — left alone it does all three at once.
  • Every node roots. Cut anywhere and both halves grow. Four stems become a dense patch within a couple of months with nothing more than scissors.
  • Floating stems shade what is below. The leaves are broad and they cover a surface fast. Keep it trimmed back if there is anything light-hungry underneath.

products.title: Bolbitis Difformis
products.body_html:
Want the Bolbitis look in a small tank? Bolbitis heteroclita var. difformis is the miniature one — finely divided lacy fronds on a compact rhizome, where the African Water Fern grows to over a foot. It attaches to wood and stone and stays in scale with a nano layout.

What You’ll Receive

Fresh, healthy Bolbitis heteroclita var. difformis cultivated and prepared by Aquarium Plants Factory®.

Bare-root Plants: Approximately 1–2 plants with loose bare roots rhizome.

Rooted Bunched: Approximately 1–2 plants secured with aquarium-safe foam and a plant weight.

Rooted Potted: Approximately 1–2 plants established in a net pot with rockwool.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Mini Bolbitis, also known as Philippine Bolbitis, Lace Bolbitis
  • Scientific name — Bolbitis heteroclita var. difformis
  • Origin — Philippines
  • Placement — Foreground to midground, on wood or stone
  • Mature height — 3–6 in
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Low to medium. Bright light means algae on slow-growing fronds
  • CO₂ — Not required, though it fills out faster with it
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Not required. Attaches to hardscape
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also suits high-humidity terrariums
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower’s Notes

  • Never bury the rhizome. Tie it to wood or stone with cotton thread or fishing line, rhizome exposed — buried in substrate it rots, and that is how most Bolbitis is lost.
  • Give it flow. This is a rheophyte from shaded Philippine streams, and moderate current keeps the fine fronds clean and moving. Still water lets detritus settle in the foliage.
  • It is slow to start. Expect several weeks before the first new frond, and avoid moving it while it settles.
  • Expect a transition period. It is usually grown emersed, and the first fronds may die back as it converts to submerged growth.
  • Divide by cutting the rhizome, leaving several fronds and some root on each section.

Want the full-size version? See Bolbitis Heudelotii (African Water Fern), which reaches 8–14 in.

products.title: Echinodorus Ozelot Green
products.body_html:
Ozelot Green is the spotted sword without the red. Broad green leaves carry the same dark mottling as the red Ozelot, so you get the pattern as texture rather than color — which makes it far easier to place in a green-dominant layout.

What You'll Receive

Fresh, healthy Echinodorus Ozelot Green cultivated and prepared by Aquarium Plants Factory®, available in convenient planting formats:

  • Bare-Root Plants: 1–2 individual plants, freshly cleaned with exposed roots, ready for planting
  • Rooted Bunched Plants: 1–2 rooted plants bundled together with a plant weight for easy placement
  • Rooted Potted Plants: 1–2 rooted plants established in a net pot with rockwool for stability

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Ozelot Green Sword
  • Scientific name — Echinodorus 'Ozelot Green'
  • Also known as — Green Ozelot Amazon Sword
  • Origin — Cultivated hybrid; parent species from South America
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Mature height — 10-16 inches
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.5-7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Heavy root feeder — nutrient-rich soil or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious rosette
  • Propagation — Adventitious plantlets on flower stalks

Grower's Notes

  • Root tabs are the whole game with swords. Ozelot Green takes almost everything it needs from the substrate. In inert gravel with liquid dosing alone it stalls and the spotting fades — which people mistake for a difficult plant rather than a hungry one.
  • The spots show best on new leaves. Mottling is strongest as a leaf emerges and softens as it matures. A well-fed plant always has patterned new growth at the center.
  • Never bury the crown. Cover the roots and leave the growing point at substrate level. A buried crown rots from the center and does not recover.
  • It propagates from flower stalks, not runners. A mature plant sends up an inflorescence carrying plantlets along its length; let each root and grow three or four leaves before separating it.
  • Green pattern is easier to place than red. A red sword forces the rest of a layout to work around it. Ozelot Green gives you the same leaf interest while staying in the green palette.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Amazon Sword & Echinodorus Care Guide.

Notes

  • As with many sword plants, older emersed leaves may naturally melt back during the transition to submerged growth. New submerged leaves will emerge as the plant acclimates to your aquarium conditions.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

Grown emersed, leaves appear green, then transform to vivid red-pink once submerged. A striking focal point for midground groups or Dutch-style "plant streets."

Care at a glance

products.title: Hygrophila Difformis (Water Wisteria) Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
The plant to put in a new tank. Hygrophila difformis — Water Wisteria — grows fast enough to soak up the nutrient surge that feeds early algae, while its finely cut lace-like leaves give a soft texture against broad-leaved plants. Forgiving, quick, and cheap to fill space with. This is the sterile Vitro Culture® format.

What You’ll Receive

Fresh Vitro Culture® Hygrophila difformis prepared by Aquarium Plants Factory®, available in multiple pack sizes.

Each portion comes in a sealed 4-inch sterile Vitro Culture® bag containing numerous young plantlets grown in nutrient gel.

1 Bag: One 4-inch Vitro Culture® bag containing multiple healthy plantlets ready for separation and planting.

5 Bags: Five 4-inch Vitro Culture® bags, ideal for filling larger aquascapes or multiple aquariums.

10 Bags: Ten 4-inch Vitro Culture® bags for large aquascaping projects or professional setups.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Water Wisteria
  • Scientific name — Hygrophila difformis
  • Also known as — Synnema triflorum
  • Origin — Indian subcontinent
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Mature height — 10–20 in
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium. Stronger light gives fuller, more compact growth
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Nutrient substrate or root tabs recommended
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower’s Notes

  • Leaf shape changes and that's normal. Tissue culture plantlets are grown emersed with simple rounded leaves. Submerged, the plant produces the deeply cut lacy foliage it's known for. New buyers often think they've been sent the wrong plant — wait for the second flush.
  • Use it as an algae counter in a new tank. Fast growth means it consumes the nutrients algae would otherwise take while slower plants establish.
  • Trim and replant tops. Every cutting roots within days, so one bag furnishes a background.
  • Space stems an inch apart. Bunched, the lower leaves shade out and drop.
  • Rinse the gel off completely before planting or it clouds water and feeds algae early on.

Notes

  • Tissue culture plants are grown emersed in sterile laboratory conditions. After planting in the aquarium, plants may transition to submerged growth and develop new leaves adapted to underwater conditions. This transition is normal and indicates healthy acclimation.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Cardamine Lyrata Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Round leaves on trailing stems, and it likes it cool. Cardamine lyrata — Japanese Cress — creeps rather than stands, sending stems with bright rounded leaves across the substrate and over driftwood. It comes from temperate East Asia and does best between 65 and 75°F, which makes it a useful choice for an unheated or lightly heated tank. This is the sterile Vitro Culture® (tissue culture) format.

What You'll Receive

  • Sold in a 4-inch sealed Vitro Culture® bag, yielding 3–4 healthy plant clusters ready for aquarium planting

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Japanese Cress
  • Scientific name — Cardamine lyrata
  • Also known as — Cardamine, Chinese Ivy
  • Origin — Temperate East Asia
  • Placement — Midground; trails over hardscape
  • Shipped size — 4-inch bag, approx. 3–4 clusters
  • Mature height — 4–10 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium. Stronger light keeps it compact rather than stretched
  • CO₂ — Not required. It grows well in low-tech tanks
  • Water — 65–75°F · pH 6.5–7.5. It prefers cooler water than most tropical plants
  • Substrate — Not required, though growth improves over a fed base
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Excellent emersed in paludariums and terrariums
  • Propagation — Cuttings — every stem section roots

Grower's Notes

  • Keep it cool. This is a temperate species, not a tropical one. Above about 78°F it stretches, thins and drops leaves. In a room-temperature or lightly heated tank it thrives — which is the opposite of most plants in this catalog.
  • Let it trail rather than planting it upright. The stems creep and drape naturally over wood and rock. Trying to grow it as a vertical stem plant fights the way it wants to grow.
  • Rinse the gel off and separate the clusters before planting, spacing them out so the runners have somewhere to go.
  • Trim regularly. It grows fast and the round leaves look best on young compact growth; older stems bare off at the base.
  • Round foliage is genuinely uncommon underwater, so it reads as contrast against the fine and strap-leaved plants most tanks already have.

Notes

  • As with all aquarium plants, Cardamine lyrata may transition from its emersed tissue culture form to submerged growth. Some initial leaf melt is normal as the plant adapts to your aquarium conditions.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Dwarf Sagittaria Subulata
products.body_html:
Want a carpet you can grow without CO₂? Dwarf Sagittaria is a grass-like rosette that spreads by runner into a dense colony, with its height set by your lighting rather than by the plant. Bright light keeps it low enough for a foreground; in dimmer tanks it stretches upward and reads as midground.

What You’ll Receive

Sold as Bare-root Plants, Bunched Plants, or Potted Plants:

  • Bare-root plants | Approx. 6 loose bare-root plants
  • Bunched plants | Approx. 6 rooted plants bundled with foam and lead weight
  • Potted plants | Approx. 6 rooted plants in a net pot with rock wool

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Dwarf Sagittaria, Dwarf Sag
  • Scientific name — Sagittaria subulata
  • Placement — Foreground to midground
  • Mature height — 4–8 in
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.5–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Root feeder — nutrient substrate or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Grows submerged or emersed
  • Propagation — Substrate runners

Grower’s Notes

  • It feeds almost entirely through its roots. In inert gravel or sand it stalls without root tabs — the most common reason it disappoints.
  • Want it short? Raise the light. Want height? Lower it. Trimming the blades doesn't control height and leaves cut ends that brown off.
  • Separate bundles into individual rosettes before planting. Bunches planted intact rot in the middle.
  • Plant each crown at the substrate line — buried crowns rot.
  • Because it is amphibious it also works in pond margins, paludariums and dry start setups. Emersed growth looks different — shorter and stiffer — and converts when submerged.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Dwarf Sagittaria Care Guide.

Notes

  • Photos are for reference; height, blade width and color vary considerably with lighting and nutrients.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Java Fern Philippine
products.body_html:
Java Fern with a straighter posture. The 'Philippine' cultivar grows long, broad fronds with a soft wave along the edge, held more upright than the standard form — so it reads as vertical structure rather than a sprawling clump. Same rhizome plant underneath: no substrate, no CO₂, no fuss.

What You'll Receive

Sold as loose bare-root plants, bunched plants, or potted plants:

  • Bare-root Plants: Approximately 6+ leaf portion, loose rhizome
  • Bunched Plants: Approximately 6+ leaf portion bundled with foam and plant weight
  • Potted Plants: Approximately 6+ leaf portion, potted in rockwool and net pot

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Philippine Java Fern
  • Scientific name — Leptochilus pteropus 'Philippine' (syn. Microsorum pteropus)
  • Also known as — Java Fern Philippine
  • Origin — Southeast Asia
  • Placement — Midground to background; attaches to driftwood and stone
  • Mature height — 8-14 inches
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — None needed; feeds from the water column
  • Growth habit — Amphibious epiphyte
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower's Notes

  • Never bury the rhizome. Tie the green horizontal stem to wood or rock with cotton thread or fishing line and leave it in open water. Buried in substrate it rots — the single most common way Java Fern is killed.
  • Black spots on old leaves are baby plants, not disease. Java Fern reproduces by growing plantlets along the leaf margins. Leave a spotted leaf in place until each plantlet has roots and two or three leaves, then detach and attach it elsewhere.
  • It grows upright, which changes where you use it. Standard Java Fern spreads outward; 'Philippine' holds height. That makes it a background plant in a small tank and a midground one in a large tank.
  • Keep the light modest. It grows slowly enough that strong lighting mostly feeds algae on the fronds. Shaded positions give cleaner, darker leaves.
  • Give it time before judging it. Emersed-grown fronds often brown off after planting. As long as the rhizome stays firm and green, submersed leaves follow — they simply take a couple of months.

  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Bolbitis Heudelotii Difformis
products.body_html:
Want the Bolbitis texture without the size? This compact 'Difformis' form grows finely dissected, ruffled fronds on a plant that stays well under a foot — the lacy structure of a full-size African Water Fern, in scale for a smaller tank.

What You’ll Receive

Available in three formats:

  • Bare-Root Plants: 4+ healthy fronds with rhizome, loose for flexible placement
  • Bunched Plants: 4+ fronds tied with foam and weight for easy setup
  • Potted Plants: 4+ fronds rooted in rockwool and net pot for secure anchoring

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Compact African Water Fern, also known as Dwarf Bolbitis
  • Scientific name — Bolbitis heteroclita var. difformis
  • Placement — Midground, on wood or stone
  • Mature height — 4–8 in
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Low to medium. High light encourages algae on slow-growing fronds
  • CO₂ — Not required, though it fills out faster with it
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5, soft to moderately hard
  • Substrate — Not required. Attaches to hardscape
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Emersed growth needs high humidity
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower’s Notes

  • Never bury the rhizome. Tie it to wood or stone with cotton thread or fishing line, rhizome exposed — buried in substrate it rots, and that is how most Bolbitis is lost.
  • Give it gentle to moderate flow. Bolbitis are rheophytes and appreciate current, but this compact form dislikes heavy turbulence — steady rather than strong.
  • It is slow to establish. Expect several weeks before the first new frond, and avoid moving it while it settles.
  • Divide by cutting the rhizome between leaf clusters, leaving several fronds and some root on each section.
  • Pairs naturally with mosses, Anubias and Bucephalandra — all shade-tolerant epiphytes with the same care needs.

Comparing our Bolbitis: the full-size Bolbitis Heudelotii reaches 8–14 in, and Bolbitis Difformis (B. heteroclita var. difformis) is the smallest at 3–6 in.

New to attaching plants? Read our guide on how to attach epiphyte plants to driftwood and rock.

Looking to buy in bulk? Get 10 or 20 plants in one order with our Bolbitis Heudelotii Difformis Bulk Pack and save 40–50% per plant.

Notes

  • As a slow-growing fern, this plant may take time to adjust and establish in new environments. Avoid burying the rhizome in substrate, as it may rot. Tie it to wood or rock with cotton thread or fishing line for best results.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Samolus Parviflorus Red Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Red that stays put. Samolus parviflorus 'Red' grows low, compact rosettes of rounded leaves that turn pink to deep red submerged — no topping, no replanting, no stems falling over. Easier to place than any red stem plant, and it prefers cooler water than most. This is the sterile Vitro Culture® format.

What You’ll Receive

Sold as a Vitro Culture® cup in a sealed 4-inch bag:

  • 4-inch Bag: Contains multiple young plants, ready for propagation and planting

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Red Samolus, Red Water Pimpernel
  • Scientific name — Samolus parviflorus 'Red'
  • Also known as — Red Lettuce
  • Placement — Foreground to midground
  • Mature height — 2–6 in
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. Intensity deepens the red
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required
  • Water — 65–78°F · pH 6.5–7.5. Note the ceiling — it prefers the cooler end
  • Substrate — Required. Root and water column feeder
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Green emersed, red submerged
  • Propagation — Side shoots and separated rosettes

Grower’s Notes

  • It arrives green. Tissue culture plantlets are grown emersed and come out of the bag pale green. The red develops over several weeks of submerged growth — judge the color then, not on arrival.
  • It prefers cooler water than most red plants. At 65–78°F it does better in a room-temperature tank than a warm tropical one.
  • As a rosette it stays where you plant it — far less work than a red stem plant that needs constant topping.
  • Separate side shoots once each has roots of its own; a couple of plants become a patch over a season.
  • Rinse the gel off completely before planting or it clouds water and feeds algae early on.

Want to go deeper? Read our guide to getting real color from red aquarium plants.

Notes

  • As with most rosette plants, Samolus parviflorus 'Red' may experience a brief adjustment period (known as "melt") after planting. Trim away melted portions and provide stable lighting, CO₂, and nutrients to encourage healthy new growth.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Bucephalandra Kedagang Red on Driftwood
products.body_html:
Kedagang Red, also known as Red Godzilla, is among the darkest reds in the Bucephalandra range — long narrow leaves with a leathery texture running deep red through bronze. This version arrives already attached to a nano piece of driftwood, so there is nothing to tie.

What You'll Receive

  • Sold as a plant on a nano driftwood.
  • Pictures are not the actual plants you will receive, but a sample representation.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Kedagang Red Buce on Driftwood
  • Scientific name — Bucephalandra sp. 'Kedagang Red'
  • Also known as — Red Godzilla, Buce Kedagang Red
  • Origin — Borneo (genus range)
  • Placement — Midground; the driftwood sits on the substrate or nestles into hardscape
  • Mature height — 2-5 inches
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium. Stronger light deepens the red, but also brings algae the plant is too slow to outgrow.
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — None needed. Epiphyte; feeds from the water column.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious rhizome creeper; grows submersed or emersed
  • Propagation — Rhizome division

Grower's Notes

  • Set the wood on the substrate, don't push it in. The rhizome is already correctly positioned above the wood. Bury it and it rots, which is the usual way an expensive Buce is lost.
  • Color builds over months. It arrives greener than the photos and darkens as it settles into submerged growth — judge it at three months, not on arrival.
  • Farm-raised, not wild-collected. All the Bucephalandra we carry is farm-grown, and much of it is raised from tissue culture rather than collected from Borneo.
  • Because the piece is loose you can move it to test placement without disturbing anything else in the tank.
  • Some leaf melt after shipping is normal. The rhizome survives and pushes new submersed leaves within a few weeks.

Godzilla and Kedagang are the same name — the color is what tells them apart. See also Pink Godzilla (Kedagang Pink) and Green Godzilla, which are different plants.

products.title: Hydrocotyle Verticillata Vitro Culture (Pennywort)
products.body_html:
Round leaves held up like small umbrellas. Hydrocotyle verticillata joins each leaf to its stalk at the center rather than the edge, so the foliage stands upright on thin stems instead of trailing flat — a shape nothing else in a planted tank produces. This is the sterile tissue culture version.

What You'll Receive

  • Sold as a Tissue Culture plants with vitamin liquid/gel
  • Bag size: Approx. 4 inches. Yield many small plants
  • Sustainable growth aquarium plants species
  • Tissue Culture Technology | 100% Free from Snail, Algae, Pathogen, and Bacteria plus Extended Shelf Life on all in Vitro Plants

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Umbrella Pennywort
  • Scientific name — Hydrocotyle verticillata
  • Also known as — Whorled Pennywort, Whorled Marshpennywort, Shield Pennywort
  • Origin — The Americas
  • Placement — Foreground to midground
  • Mature height — 4-8 inches
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium to high
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — Nutrient-rich soil or root tabs; also feeds from the water column
  • Growth habit — Amphibious creeping stem
  • Propagation — Runners

Grower's Notes

  • Bare stalks with few leaves means not enough light. Under weak lighting the stems stretch upward and the umbrella leaves thin out. Raise the intensity or move it forward rather than dosing more fertilizer.
  • Separate the culture into small clusters. Rinse the gel off and plant a few plantlets per spot, an inch apart. Runners close the gaps far faster than one clump grows outward.
  • Trim at the substrate to hold a boundary. Runners spread quickly and will cross into whatever is planted next to it. A trim every few weeks keeps the patch where you put it.
  • Every node roots. Cut sections anywhere and pin them down with plant weights until they anchor. It is one of the easiest plants in the catalog to multiply.
  • The upright leaf on a central stalk is the identifying feature — useful for telling this apart from the flat-creeping Hydrocotyle tripartita, which is a different plant entirely.

Notes

  • Pictures are not the actual plants you will receive, but a sample representation. Unless specific, we don't guarantee aquatic plants will be free of pests, and pesticides, grow emerged, or submerge.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Anubias Petite Snow White Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Cream-white marbling on leaves under an inch across. Anubias sp. 'Petite Snow White' is one of the most heavily variegated Anubias in the hobby — and, for exactly that reason, one of the least forgiving. This is the sterile tissue-culture format.

What You'll Receive

  • One (1) Vitro Culture® 4-inch bag of Anubias sp. 'Petite Snow White'
  • Yield: Approximately 3–4 small young plants, ready to plant or attach to hardscape

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Petite Snow White Anubias
  • Scientific name — Anubias sp. 'Petite Snow White'
  • Origin — Cultivated hybrid; the genus is native to West and Central Africa
  • Placement — Midground, attached to hardscape
  • Mature height — 2-4 inches
  • Growth rate — Very slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Advanced
  • Light — Low to medium. Excess light burns the pale tissue and feeds algae — the single most common way this plant is lost.
  • CO₂ — Not required. Improves vigor under otherwise stable conditions.
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5. Stability matters more than any particular value.
  • Substrate — Not required. Epiphyte; attaches to wood or stone.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious; also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Rhizome division, once well established

Grower's Notes

  • Cream-white tissue carries no chlorophyll, which is what makes this Advanced. The more white a leaf holds, the less energy the plant produces — so it grows very slowly, recovers badly from damage, and cannot outgrow algae on the pale areas. Anubias is famously indestructible; this cultivar is the exception that proves it.
  • It can revert. Heavily variegated Anubias sometimes starts pushing plain green leaves. Remove fully green shoots promptly — green tissue photosynthesizes better and will gradually take the plant over if left.
  • Never bury the rhizome. Tie it to wood or stone and leave it exposed; buried rhizomes rot, and this plant will not grow back from that quickly.
  • Rinse the gel off gently with aquarium or dechlorinated water — not tap — and separate the plantlets before attaching.
  • The sterile format matters more here than on a hardy plant: an algae outbreak arriving with the plant is very hard to clear from white leaves that grow this slowly.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Anubias Care Guide.

Notes

Pictures shown are for reference only. Actual plant size, shape, and variegation pattern may vary depending on growing conditions. This Vitro Culture® bag is sealed for freshness — please follow proper sterilization and acclimation procedures upon opening.

Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Cryptocoryne Retrospiralis Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Tall, ribbon-like leaves that twist along their length. Cryptocoryne retrospiralis is one of the few crypts that works as a background plant — it gives a planted tank vertical movement without the trimming a stem plant demands. This is the sterile Vitro Culture® format.

What You'll Receive

  • 1x Cryptocoryne Retrospiralis Vitro Culture® — grown in 4-inch bag
  • Yields approx. 3–4 healthy young plants ready for planting

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Retrospiralis Crypt, also known as Spiral Water Trumpet
  • Scientific name — Cryptocoryne retrospiralis
  • Origin — India
  • Placement — Background
  • Mature height — 10-16 inches
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium
  • CO₂ — Not required, though it speeds establishment
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.5-7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Root feeder — nutrient substrate or root tabs under the crown.
  • Growth habit — Amphibious rosette; also grows emersed, so it suits paludariums
  • Propagation — Runners

Grower's Notes

  • A background plant that does not need cutting. Stem plants reach the surface and then need weekly trimming. Retrospiralis grows to height and stops, which is the entire argument for using a crypt at the back of a low-maintenance tank.
  • Crypt melt is expected and is not failure. Tissue culture plantlets shed their emersed leaves as they convert to submersed growth. Leave the roots undisturbed — new leaves come from the crown within three to six weeks.
  • Plant the crown at substrate level. Bury the roots and leave the growing point exposed. A buried crown rots from the center.
  • Feed the roots and give it depth. A tall crypt needs a deep, well-fed substrate to anchor and fuel 16 inches of leaf. Root tabs or aquasoil; two inches of substrate minimum.
  • It spreads by runner. Once settled it sends up new plants around the mother — leave space behind it and the stand thickens on its own over a year or two.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Cryptocoryne Care Guide.

Notes

Like many Cryptocoryne species, Cryptocoryne retrospiralis may undergo a temporary "crypt melt" when adapting to a new aquarium environment. This is a normal process. Once established, new growth will emerge and the plant will stabilize.

Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Ludwigia Glandulosa (Peruensis)
products.body_html:
Want burgundy rather than scarlet? Ludwigia glandulosa runs deep wine-red to purple on narrow lance-shaped leaves held on stiff upright stems. It is one of the darker reds available, and it grows straight up with almost no branching — which makes it unusually easy to place.

You may know it as Ludwigia peruensis. That is a trade name — see the note below.

What You’ll Receive

Sold as loose fresh-cut plants, bunched plants, or potted plants:

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Approx. 6 individual loose-cut stems without root.
  • Bunched Plants: Approx. 6 stems without root, bundled with foam and plant weight.
  • Potted Plants: Approx. 6 stems without root, potted in rockwool and a net pot.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Ludwigia Peruensis, also known as Cylindricfruit Primrose-Willow
  • Scientific name — Ludwigia glandulosa
  • Also known as — Ludwigia peruensis, Ludwigia perennis, Ludwigia cylindrica (all misapplied)
  • Origin — Southeastern United States
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 in
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Why several names?

This plant has been sold as Ludwigia peruensis and Ludwigia perennis for years, and both names are still in wide use. Neither is correct — the plant is Ludwigia glandulosa, a species from the wetlands of the southeastern United States, not from Peru.

You are buying the same plant you have always known as Peruensis, correctly named.

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. Intensity decides whether you get wine-red or olive-green
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Root and water column feeder, hungry for iron
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower’s Notes

  • It barely branches on its own. Stems grow straight up with minimal side shoots until you cut the main stem — then lateral shoots form. If you want a dense stand rather than isolated poles, topping is not optional.
  • In lower light the leaves go olive-green with red undersides, which is a two-toned effect worth having in its own right. The wine-red only appears under strong light.
  • It sheds lower leaves when light is insufficient. Bare stems near the substrate mean light isn't reaching them, not a nutrient problem.
  • Iron and steady micronutrients matter more here than for most Ludwigia.
  • Often confused with Ludwigia senegalensis, which carries a visible vein pattern this one lacks.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Ludwigia Care Guide.

Notes

  • Pictures shown are sample representations and not the exact plants you will receive. Unless otherwise specified, we do not guarantee aquatic plants will be free of pests or pesticides, nor whether they are grown emersed or submerged.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Ludwigia Rubin
products.body_html:
Most deep red stem plants demand a high-tech tank before they show any color. Ludwigia Rubin does not. Broad, spade-shaped leaves turn wine red on both surfaces under medium light with no CO₂ at all, which makes it the shortest route to a red midground in a low-tech tank.

What You'll Receive

Fresh, healthy Ludwigia Rubin cultivated and prepared by Aquarium Plants Factory®, available in convenient planting formats.

  • Fresh-cut Plants: Approximately 6+ loose, fresh-cut stems without roots.
  • Fresh-cut Bunched: Approximately 6+ stems bundled with foam and a plant weight for easy planting.
  • Fresh-cut Potted: Approximately 6+ stems securely potted in a net pot with rockwool for stability and convenient planting.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Ludwigia Rubin
  • Scientific name — Ludwigia repens 'Rubin'
  • Also known as — Red Diamond, Ludwigia Ruby
  • Origin — Cultivated form of a North and Central American species
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6+ fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 inches
  • Mature height — 6-16 inches
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Medium to high
  • CO₂ — Not required. It reddens without injection, which is the whole point of this cultivar
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich soil or root tabs, plus water column dosing
  • Growth habit — Amphibious stem, feeds from roots and water column
  • Propagation — Cuttings

Grower's Notes

  • This is the red plant to start with. Most reds need high light and injected CO₂ before they color. Rubin does it on medium light in a low-tech tank — if earlier attempts at a red plant have failed, this is the one that changes that.
  • Both leaf surfaces color up. Unlike Ludwigia repens, which stays green on top and red underneath, Rubin holds red through the whole leaf. That is why it reads as a solid block of color from the front of the tank.
  • Low nitrate deepens it, but do not starve it. Rubin darkens when nitrate is kept modest and iron is dosed consistently. Cutting nitrate to zero stalls the plant instead — aim for lean but present.
  • Trim above a node and replant the cutting. Each cut stem branches into two, so repeated trimming builds a dense red thicket rather than a row of single stems.
  • Emersed stock changes shape after planting. Leaves grown out of water are thicker and often greener. The first submersed leaves are broader and considerably redder, so judge the plant by its new growth.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Ludwigia Care Guide.

Notes

  • Aquarium plants are living organisms and may naturally vary in size, shape, and coloration depending on season, lighting, and growing conditions. Most plants are grown emersed before shipping and will gradually transition to their submerged form after being introduced into the aquarium.
  • Never release aquarium plants into natural waterways.

products.title: Alternanthera Reineckii
products.body_html:
The benchmark red stem plant. Alternanthera reineckii — Scarlet Temple, or simply AR — grows broad leaves with green tops and deep red-to-purple undersides on upright bushy stems. It is the plant most people mean when they say they want red in a planted tank, and unlike many red stems it will color without pressurized CO₂.

What You’ll Receive

Enhance your aquarium with our versatile selection of high-quality aquatic plants, available in three convenient formats:

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Includes approximately 6+ loose, fresh-cut stems without roots. Perfect for flexible planting arrangements.
  • Fresh-Cut Bunched: Approximately 6+ fresh-cut stems without roots, bundled with foam and a plant weight for easy placement.
  • Fresh-Cut Potted: About 6+ fresh-cut stems without roots, securely potted in a net pot with rockwool, ensuring stability and healthy growth.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Scarlet Temple
  • Scientific name — Alternanthera reineckii
  • Also known as — AR, Telanthera rosefolia
  • Origin — South America
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6+ fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 in
  • Mature height — 8–16 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate
  • Light — Medium to high. Color intensity tracks light
  • CO₂ — Recommended, not required
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich substrate
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower’s Notes

  • Red on a budget of light, not CO₂. Rotala and Ludwigia reds usually want gas and nitrate management. AR colors mainly on light intensity and iron, which puts real red within reach of a medium-light tank.
  • The color sits on the leaf undersides. Position it where light rakes across the group rather than straight down.
  • Trim and replant tops repeatedly — that's what turns six stems into the dense red block people buy this plant for.
  • It feeds at the roots as well as the water column, so root tabs plus regular dosing beat either alone.
  • Other forms in the range: Rosanervig for pink veining at the same 8-16 inch size, Super Magenta for deeper color, or the 3-5 inch dwarfs AR Mini and Rosanervig Mini for nano tanks.

products.body_html:
Looking for pink without the bulk? Alternanthera reineckii 'Pink Sunset' is a mutation of Alternanthera reineckii that our nursery first introduced to the United States in 2021. It reads like Alternanthera reineckii 'Rosanervig' at a glance, but the stems are finer and the leaves noticeably narrower — a lighter, more delicate texture in the same color range.

Choose from our selection of fresh, nursery-grown Alternanthera reineckii ‘Pink Sunset’:

  • Loose Fresh-Cut Plants: Approximately 6 unrooted, freshly trimmed stems.
  • Fresh Cut Bunched: About 6 stems, neatly bundled with foam and a plant weight, without root.
  • Potted Plants: Around 6 fresh-cut stems, without root in a net pot with rock wool.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Pink Sunset Alternanthera
  • Scientific name — Alternanthera reineckii 'Pink Sunset'
  • Also known as — AR Pink Sunset
  • Origin — Cultivar; introduced by Aquarium Plants Factory nursery (U.S.A., 2021)
  • Placement — Midground
  • Shipped size — Approx. 6 fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 in
  • Mature height — 8–16 in

Care

  • Difficulty — Intermediate

Grower’s Notes

  • Narrower leaves change how it plants. Standard Alternanthera reineckii makes broad blocks of color. Pink Sunset's finer stems let you use pink as an accent inside a group rather than as a wall of it.
  • The color lives on the leaf underside. Position it where the light rakes across rather than straight down, and the magenta actually shows.
  • Trim and replant tops rather than letting stems run tall. Repeated topping is what turns three stems into a dense group.
  • It feeds both at the roots and from the water column, so root tabs plus regular dosing outperform either alone.
  • Some fading and leaf drop during acclimation is normal; new growth returns to color once light and nutrients are steady.

products.title: Pogostemon Stellatus
products.body_html:
A starburst at every node. Pogostemon stellatus whorls fine needle-like leaves around the stem so each node opens like a small explosion, and under strong light with CO₂ the whole plant shifts from green through pink and purple into orange. It is one of the most striking stem plants in the hobby and one of the least tolerant of an unstable tank.

What You’ll Receive

Sold as loose fresh-cut plants, bunched plants, or potted plants:

  • Fresh-Cut Plants: Approx. 5 stems, loose fresh-cut stems without root
  • Bunched Plants: Approx. 5 fresh-cut stems without root, bundled with foam and a plant weight
  • Potted Plants: Approx. 5 fresh-cut stems without root, potted in rockwool and net pot

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Pogostemon Stellatus
  • Scientific name — Pogostemon stellatus
  • Also known as — Eusteralis stellata, Star Pogostemon
  • Origin — Southeast Asia and Australia
  • Placement — Background
  • Shipped size — Approx. 5 fresh-cut stems, roughly 4-8 in
  • Mature height — 10–20 in
  • Suits — 20 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Advanced
  • Light — High. Both the color and the compact form depend on it
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 72–82°F · pH 6.0–7.0
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich substrate
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant top cuttings or side shoots

Grower’s Notes

  • Stability matters more than any single parameter. Stellatus reacts to swings in CO₂, light period or fertilisation faster than almost anything else in the tank — it will drop leaves in a week from a change others shrug off. Set the tank up first, then add this plant.
  • Melt after shipping is normal and can look total. Leave the stems planted; new growth comes from the nodes.
  • Trim the tops and replant them; side shoots from the trimmed stem thicken the group.
  • Plant stems individually an inch apart. Bunched, the lower stems shade out and rot.
  • Want the leaf texture without the demands? Pogostemon Octopus keeps a similar form and stays green, and Pogostemon Deccanensis is a far more forgiving background plant.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Pogostemon Care Guide.

  • Pogostemon stellatus is a sensitive species that may melt or lose leaves during shipping or acclimation. Stable parameters, high light, and CO₂ injection are key to long-term success.

products.title: Vallisneria Torta
products.body_html:
Want a corkscrew Val that stays small? Vallisneria torta is the shortest of the twisted Vallisneria — light green, almost translucent spiral leaves reaching only about 8 inches, which makes it the only one that works in a nano tank or a genuine foreground.

What You’ll Receive

  • Sold as Bare-root Plants, Bunched plants, or Potted plants
  • Bare-root plants | approx. 2-3 loose, bare-root plants
  • Bunched plants | approx. 2-3 rooted plants with foam, and lead weight
  • Potted plants | approx. 2-3 rooted plants with net pot and rock wool

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Torta Val, also known as Corkscrew Val
  • Scientific name — Vallisneria torta
  • Also known as — Vallisneria asiatica var. biwaensis (the identity is not firmly settled, and nurseries sell it as Torta)
  • Origin — Asia
  • Placement — Foreground to midground
  • Shipped size — Approx. 2-3 plants, roughly 3-6 in
  • Mature height — 4–8 in
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Fast

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium. Brighter light tightens the spiral
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 68–82°F · pH 6.5–8.0. Tolerates hard, alkaline water well
  • Substrate — Required. Root feeder — nutrient substrate or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Fully aquatic
  • Propagation — Substrate runners

Grower’s Notes

  • This is the small one. Most Vallisneria run to the surface and trail along it. Torta tops out around eight inches, so it works as a foreground or midground group and suits nano tanks — the only twisted Val that does.
  • Plant the crown at the substrate line, never below it. A buried crown rots — the usual reason a new Val fails in the first fortnight.
  • Feed at the roots. In inert gravel it survives but barely spreads.
  • Don't trim the tops to control height. Cut Val leaves brown at the cut — remove whole leaves at the base instead.
  • Runners travel fast. Pull unwanted plantlets by hand rather than cutting them.

Choosing between our twisted Vallisneria

  • Vallisneria torta (this plant) — shortest, 4–8 in, midground and nano tanks.
  • Vallisneria americana 'Asiatica' — 8–12 in, with a wider twisted blade.
  • Vallisneria 'Contortionist' — 10–20 in, with a narrower twisted blade. Background.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Vallisneria Care Guide.

products.title: Butterfly Moss
products.body_html:
Moss you can actually see the leaves on. Butterfly Moss (Plagiomnium sp. 'Butterfly') grows rounded, overlapping leaves along creeping stems — wing-like and large enough to read as foliage, where Java Moss and Christmas Moss are a fine green haze. It's the moss to use when you want structure rather than fuzz.

What You’ll Receive

  • Loose Portion: A small loose portion of Butterfly Moss, approximately 2" x 2" in size
  • Ready to Attach: Tie it to hardscape with cotton thread or press it under mesh; it will self-adhere over time
  • Note: Occasionally may include a mix of other moss species due to its delicate nature

Plant Profile

  • Common name — Butterfly Moss
  • Scientific name — Plagiomnium sp. 'Butterfly'
  • Placement — Midground, attached to wood, stone or mesh
  • Mature height — 2–4 in
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Beginner
  • Light — Low to medium. Intense light bleaches it and invites algae
  • CO₂ — Not required
  • Water — 68–78°F · pH 6.0–7.5. Note the ceiling — this moss prefers cooler water than most tropical plants
  • Substrate — Not required. Attaches to hardscape
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Fragmentation — divide and re-attach

Grower’s Notes

  • Keep it under 78°F. Plagiomnium comes from cooler, shaded, damp habitats. In a tank running at 80–82°F it thins out and browns — the single most common reason this moss disappoints. Pair it with cooler-water species rather than discus.
  • The hair-like growths at the base are rhizoids, not algae. They're how the moss anchors itself — leave them.
  • Tie it on thinly with cotton thread. Thick mats trap detritus and rot from underneath; a thin layer grows across the surface instead.
  • It is a true moss, not a liverwort, despite the leafy appearance.
  • Slow growth means it holds a shape for months without trimming — useful on a moss wall where faster species need constant cutting.

Looking to buy in bulk? Get 10 or 20 portions in one order with our Butterfly Moss Bulk Pack and save 40–50% per portion.

Want to go deeper? Read our Butterfly Moss guide, or our guide to aquarium moss varieties.

products.title: Bacopa Platinum Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Almost no green at all. Bacopa monnieri 'Platinum' is the albino form of the toughest stem plant in the hobby — white to palest cream foliage against dark substrate. This is the sterile Vitro Culture® format, which matters more here than on most plants: an algae outbreak introduced with the plant is very hard to recover from on foliage this slow and this pale.

What You'll Receive

  • Sold as a Tissue Culture package with vitamin liquid/gel
  • Package size: Approx. 4 inches
  • Sustainable growth aquarium plant species
  • Great value! Nice specimen!
  • Tissue Culture Technology | 100% Free from Snail, Algae, Pathogen, and Bacteria plus Extended Shelf Life on all in Vitro Plants

Plant Profile

  • Common name — White Moneywort, White Water Hyssop
  • Scientific name — Bacopa monnieri 'Platinum'
  • Also known as — Bacopa Platinum
  • Origin — Cultivated form; the species is pantropical
  • Placement — Midground to background
  • Shipped size — Small tissue-cultured plantlets, roughly 1-2 inches
  • Mature height — 6-12 inches
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Slow

Care

  • Difficulty — Advanced
  • Light — Medium to high. Under weak light it stretches thin and pale reaching for more
  • CO₂ — Required. With almost no chlorophyll, it needs every advantage available
  • Water — 72-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5. Stability matters more than any specific value
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich substrate plus regular water column dosing
  • Growth habit — Amphibious. Also grows emersed
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower's Notes

  • White tissue cannot photosynthesize. That is the whole difficulty in one sentence. Plain Bacopa monnieri survives neglect because it produces energy efficiently; Platinum produces almost none, so every other condition has to compensate.
  • It can revert to green. Green shoots photosynthesize properly and will outgrow the white growth if left. Cut them out at the base to keep the stand white.
  • Strong light keeps it low and creeping; weak light makes it stretch and thin. Neither is unhealthy, but only one looks like the photographs.
  • Separate the plantlets and plant them an inch apart, and rinse the gel off completely — on a plant this slow, gel-fed algae in the first weeks is hard to reverse.
  • Also available as loose fresh-cut stems if you want larger plants immediately.

products.title: Hydrocotyle Tripartita Mini
products.body_html:
Half the leaf, half the height. Hydrocotyle tripartita 'Mini' is a dwarf form of the standard clover pennywort — same three-lobed leaves and fast creeping runners, but small enough to stay flat at 1–2 inches instead of climbing. In a nano tank, that difference is what makes it a carpet rather than a shrub.

  • Scientific name — Hydrocotyle tripartita 'Mini'

products.title: Staurogyne Repens White Albino Vitro Culture
products.body_html:
Staurogyne repens is one of the most reliable low carpeting plants in the hobby. The 'White Albino' form takes that familiar shape and strips almost all the green out of it, leaving pale ivory foliage that glows against dark substrate. Less chlorophyll means less energy, so it asks for considerably more than the standard form.

What You'll Receive

One 4-inch sealed Vitro Culture® bag containing healthy Staurogyne Repens 'White Albino' plantlets—ready to rinse, acclimate, and plant with care.

Plant Profile

  • Common name — White Albino Staurogyne
  • Scientific name — Staurogyne repens 'White Albino'
  • Also known as — Staurogyne repens 'Variegated'
  • Origin — Cultivated form; the species comes from the Rio Cristalino, Brazil
  • Placement — Foreground to midground
  • Shipped size — Small tissue-cultured plantlets, roughly 1-2 inches
  • Mature height — 2-4 inches
  • Suits — 10 gallons and up
  • Growth rate — Medium

Care

  • Difficulty — Advanced
  • Light — Medium. Note the ceiling — strong light bleaches pale tissue
  • CO₂ — Recommended
  • Water — 68-82°F, pH 6.0-7.5
  • Substrate — Required. Nutrient-rich soil or root tabs
  • Growth habit — Amphibious creeping stem
  • Propagation — Cuttings — trim and replant stem tops

Grower's Notes

  • Pale tissue burns before green tissue does. Do not treat "needs light" as "needs more light". Medium intensity is the target — strong light bleaches the ivory leaves and algae takes hold on them long before it touches anything green in the tank.
  • Reverted green shoots will appear. Any pale sport can throw fully green growth, and green grows faster. Cut those stems out at the base as soon as you spot them or they will take over the group.
  • Feed the substrate. With reduced pigment the plant cannot afford an inefficient root zone. Aquasoil or root tabs under the planting area make the difference between slow and stalled.
  • Plant small portions, spaced out. Rinse the gel off and separate the culture into groups of two or three plantlets an inch apart. Dense clumps shade their own bases, which this plant recovers from poorly.
  • Want the same carpet without the difficulty? Standard Staurogyne repens is a Beginner plant with the same shape and growth habit — the albino form is a collector's plant, not a workhorse.

Want to go deeper? Read our complete Staurogyne Repens Care Guide.

Notes

  • Photos shown are sample representations. Actual plant appearance may vary depending on lighting, CO₂, and care. This albino variant is fragile and may melt if not given proper light and nutrients. Not recommended for beginners.
